title: [D0 Foundations] Structured local logging with credential redaction
summary: `helena.observability` now exists: one log channel writing one JSON object per line to stderr with ten fixed top-level keys (timestamp, level, component, event, tenant, sensor, event_id, context_id, versions, fields), identity taken from Settings with no default, and a `Redactor` that removes credentials by registered value and by URL structure. Redaction runs at the emitter, not at the call site — every value is swept before serialization, `outbound_request` and `exception` route the request URL through `Redactor.url`, and the serialized line is swept once more before it is written. A boundary test keeps every hosted tracing/telemetry SDK undeclared, unimported and unresolvable in the environment, and a second test forbids `print()` and stdlib `logging` inside the package so there is one logging path.
assumption_validated: That a credential travelling in a URL path can be kept out of every log line by a mechanism at the emitter rather than by discipline at each call site — and that the exception path is a real leak, not a hypothetical one. Both confirmed by execution. `urllib.error.HTTPError.url` carries the whole request URL including a path-embedded key while `str(exception)` does not, so an exception logged by its attributes leaks and one logged by its message does not; verified against a real 404 from the live abuse.ch host and against a real local HTTP server inside the suite. A real fetch with the real ABUSECH_AUTH_KEY in the path, logged through this module, emitted `https://threatfox.abuse.ch/export/***redacted***/json/recent/` on both the request line and the failure line, with the key absent from the output. A negative result alongside it: the current ThreatFox bulk export does NOT take the key in the URL path — `https://threatfox.abuse.ch/export/json/recent/` answered 200 with no credential at all, and both key-in-path shapes answered 404.
makes_buildable: Every later increment has a log channel it does not have to design: `logger(component, settings)` gives a StructuredLogger carrying tenant and sensor, and `log.outbound_request(...)` / `log.exception(...)` are the two calls a feed loader or an MCP provider tool makes around a fetch. `Redactor.url` is the helper the loader uses on the URL it records as provenance, so the provenance row and the log line are redacted by the same code. The D1 normalizer has `event_id` and the D2 context builder has `context_id` as first-class record fields, and anything citing versions has `versions`. The hosted-tracing boundary test means the LangChain/model-client increment cannot pull a tracer in transitively without failing the suite.

verification.detail: 121 passed, up from 100 (53 of them in tests/test_observability.py). `make check` green: `uv lock --check` clean (no dependency added), sources compile, suite passes. The exception path is exercised against a real urllib request to a real http.server on 127.0.0.1 — a real HTTPError, not a hand-built one — and one test asserts the premise directly (the key IS in `error.url`, and is NOT in `str(error)`), so the redaction assertions cannot pass vacuously. Two tests use the real key from the local `.env` and assert on a precomputed boolean with a fixed message, never on the value, so a failure cannot print it. Separately and outside the suite, one live request to threatfox.abuse.ch with the real key in the path was logged through the module and the emitted lines inspected: no key, marker present on both lines. No SQL in this increment, so nothing to execute against an engine instance.

escalations.detail: tests/test_package_layout.py SUPPORT_MODULES gained "observability" alongside "config". Observability is not an eighth architecture component: concept/07-principles.md gives it its own section rather than a place in the pipeline, and every component logs. The friction task 0 built is intact — an unexpected module still fails the assertion.

tests/test_dependency_boundary.py gained HOSTED_TELEMETRY_DISTRIBUTIONS (17 entries: langsmith, langfuse, opentelemetry-{sdk,api}, sentry-sdk, ddtrace, datadog, newrelic, elastic-apm, logfire, libhoney, openinference-instrumentation, arize-phoenix, braintrust, wandb, mlflow, helicone) and two tests. The list is a judgement call about which SDKs count as hosted telemetry; prometheus-client was deliberately left off because a local scrape endpoint is not an egress channel. The stronger of the two tests asserts the modules do not RESOLVE in the environment at all, not merely that they are undeclared — so a tracer arriving transitively fails the suite. If a future approved dependency drags one in, that test is where it surfaces, and the answer is a recorded decision, not an exemption.

CONTEXT.md §3 and concept/05-threat-intelligence.md both state that the abuse.ch key travels in the URL path for the bulk export. Checked against the artifact: https://threatfox.abuse.ch/export/json/recent/ returns 200 with NO credential, and both plausible key-in-path shapes return 404. So the specific claim about that endpoint does not hold today. The redaction rule is retained unchanged and is not weakened by this — the concept records that a live key already reached a project conversation inside a pasted link, and HTTPError.url leaks whatever URL you requested regardless of who requires what. But the feed-loader increment must establish the current bulk endpoint and its auth mechanism for itself rather than inherit the assumption. Not blocking: this task's job was the redactor, not the loader.

deferred: "Route EVERY outbound-request log and every exception carrying a request URL through the redactor" — the mechanism is built and is the only way to log a request, but there is no outbound request anywhere in the package yet (no HTTP client, no loader, no model call), so there are zero call sites to route. What enforces the rule for future call sites is the emitter-level sweep plus the one-logging-path test, not a review of call sites that do not exist. The increment that adds the first fetch owns using `outbound_request` and `exception` rather than `info` with a raw URL.

Routing third-party stdlib `logging` records (psycopg, confluent-kafka) into this channel, or silencing them. No handler is configured, so their records currently go nowhere. Belongs to the increment that first runs one of those clients against a real service.
A log level below `info` and any level filtering or sampling. LEVELS is (info, warning, error); a level nothing emits is a config key with one value.

Binding event_id/context_id onto a logger once instead of passing them per call. Every call site is explicit for now; a `.bound()` helper is worth adding when a stage actually logs in a loop over one context.

Any counter or metric surface. `concept/07-principles.md` requires latency, cost, staleness, error, escalation and record counts to be observable, but those are typed columns on stored rows — the store, not the log — and the tables do not exist yet.
lessons: task 02: `urllib.error.HTTPError` carries the full request URL on `.url` and `.filename` but NOT in `str(exception)`. So logging an exception's message is safe and logging its attributes or its repr is not — which is the opposite of the intuition that the message is the risky part. Verified against a real 404.

task 02: An `HTTPError` IS the response object and holds the connection open. Returning one from a helper without calling `.close()` leaves an unclosed socket, and because pytest is configured with `filterwarnings = ["error"]` the resulting ResourceWarning surfaces as an unraisable-exception failure in whatever test happens to run later — in this session, an unrelated AST test. If a test fails with PytestUnraisableExceptionWarning about a socket, look for an unclosed urllib response, not at the test that failed.

task 02: `urllib.parse.urlencode` percent-encodes `*`, so a redaction marker rebuilt through it comes out as `%2A%2A%2Aredacted%2A%2A%2A`. Pass `safe="*"` to keep `***redacted***` readable in a log line.

task 02: Redacting a URL structurally must NOT guess at path segments. This project fetches URLs whose path segments are sha256 hashes (mb-api.abuse.ch/downloads/<sha256>/), and an entropy or length heuristic would redact exactly the provenance the fetch exists to record. Redaction of a path segment is by registered value only; the stated consequence is that an unregistered credential in a path is not redacted, and the answer to that is that credentials only enter through helena.config.

task 02: A test that asserts a real credential is absent must not put the credential in the assertion expression — pytest's assertion rewriting prints both operands on failure, so `assert key not in output` leaks the key at the exact moment the redaction failed. Compute the boolean first: `leaked = key in output; assert not leaked, "..."`.

task 02: The current ThreatFox bulk export at https://threatfox.abuse.ch/export/json/recent/ serves 200 with no credential at all. Combined with task 01's finding that the API v1 wants an `Auth-Key` HEADER, there is currently no confirmed abuse.ch endpoint that takes the key in the URL path. Do not build the loader around one without fetching first.
failed_approaches: task 02: Applying the embedded-URL regex to the already-serialized JSON line was considered and rejected before it was written: with `separators=(",",":")` there is no whitespace between a URL value and the next key, so `\S+` would swallow `","level":"info"}` into the match and mangle the record. Structural URL redaction is applied to values before serialization; only the structure-blind literal sweep runs over the line.
next_session_should_know: Log through `helena.observability.logger(component, settings)` and nothing else — `print()` and stdlib `logging` inside `helena` are a test failure (tests/test_observability.py::test_the_package_has_no_second_logging_path), and so is importing or installing any hosted tracing SDK (tests/test_dependency_boundary.py, two tests). The record has ten fixed top-level keys; your own fields are keyword arguments and land nested under `fields`, so you cannot shadow `tenant`. `event` is the dotted name of what happened; `event_id` is the normalizer's flow-event identity and `context_id` the host-context identity, both keyword arguments, both null when absent. `versions={}` raises — pass the real version set or omit it. A field that will not JSON-serialize raises TypeError rather than being repr'd, so convert datetimes at the call site. For anything with a URL: `log.outbound_request(event, method=..., url=...)` and `log.exception(event, exc, ...)` — never `log.info(..., url=raw_url)`, even though the emitter would catch a configured credential anyway. `Redactor.url(...)` is also the helper for the provenance URL a loader stores, so the row and the log line get identical treatment; build one with `Redactor.from_settings(settings)`. Two things the next sessions own that this task surfaced: the abuse.ch bulk endpoint really does not take the key in the path today (see escalations — fetch before building the loader), and stdlib `logging` from psycopg/confluent-kafka is unrouted. Still open and untouched since task 0: the concept/05 vs data/netify tension, bin/README.md's dangling reference to scripts/build-binaries.sh, and there is still no git repository.
